x: John Bicourt was the first Bel home after having been pushed hard by ever-green Pat Newall making one of his all too infrequent performances.

Pat Newall chivvied up our leading men with a snappy 28:49, just 14 seconds faster than his winning time of 12 years ago! Lionel Mann and Pat O'Connor both ran exceptionally well and you will be hearing a lot more of this fast improving pair.

Trevor Hart was our best performer for the 'A' team and Pat Newall the top 'B' man. The wisdom of racing on the track between the National C.C. and Relay events was shown to be doubtful when both Gerry Williams (strained stomach muscle) and Gerry North (strained calf) were invalids at the A.A.A. ina…
Clive Shippen had moved through after a bad patch and had taken Pat Newall with him, and the two Belgravians steadily consolidated their positions for the rest of the race to finish 9th and 10th.
He took the 880 yards ahead of Bob Taylor and Malcolm Robinson, the mile from Pat Newall and Ranjit Bhatia and the three miles, in 14:25, after sitting in on Newall for nearly the full distance.

Charlie Walker, getting fitter with every race, and Pat Newall, making a welcome return to Belgrave colours, both ran outstanding races. Denis Jones kindly made up the scoring three and thoroughly deserved his silver medal.

Arthur Bruce on the first stage was rather unfit and both Pat Newall and Charlie Walker ran slightly below their recent excellent form. Not enough hills on Clapham Common where they do their training!

Standing: John Wasbrough, Charlie Walker, Alan Lane, Rex Bale, Keith Duckett, Mark Hutton, Tony Stone, Derek Manning, Dudley Gordon. Kneeling: Paul King, Arthur Bruce, Leo Coy, Frank Barrett, Charlie Dickinson, Mike Newton, Pat Newall and Harry Porter.
